text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Packs Talon 11 Backpack, Flame Orange, Small/Medium I love this pack for hiking. Can't really fault it for anything. Only complaint is water bladder is a bit of a struggle to get inserted with water in it, even without water it's a bit tough. You just have to believe with all your heart that it will go in and it will, eventually.

I like the pack so much, I bought it's bigger brother the Talon 22. I really like the multiple ways I can lash my trekking poles to it and how useful the bungy cinch area is for carrying a variety of items. I used it recently to carry a litter sized water bottle when I needed more water than my bladder could carry.

I'm 6' and the M/L is plenty long. One of the reasons I got this pack is because of the two sizes available, and nice hip belt that can be hard to find on a small pack. In fact it's hard to find a real hiking pack in such a small size.

I bought a used one first and the buckle for the helmet holder/bungy cords was broken. The plastic seemed really flimsy. But the buckle on the new pack was much better. So give that buckle a few good squeezes to make sure you have a good buckle before heading out. Might be good to check all of them, if some aren't getting molded right.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Packs Talon 11 Backpack, Flame Orange, Small/Medium

text_fidelity_a:
Zumba Fitness Tone Up DVD System New Years resolutions anyone? This boxed set has everything you need to get started on a fitness program. The first thing you notice when you open the kit is the weights. They are shakers. How fun is that? Two booklets are included.One, the program guide, offers a schedule for using the workouts. I don't know about you, but doing the same thing every day bores me. That's not a problem with this set. The program guide suggests using different workout routines every day of the week, with a day of rest after each two days of workouts. The exercise choreography itself is not only sound for building fitness, it's also witty, imaginative, and lots of fun. I'm out of shape, so I have to modify the movements a lot, but the instructors are excellent and work into each movement slowly, pointing out correct form to avoid injury. My room is very small, and some of the dance moves do take a little more space than I have. It's not just standing in one spot, but I am still able to do them. The chair routines are fantastic. They are designed for your upper body and abs, but you really get a full body workout.

Also included is a booklet with a great nutrition guide. It has a full week's worth of meals with recipes, and it's small enough to stick in your purse or pocket when you go to the store. The meals feature the latest weight-loss and cardiac health superstars, but everything you need will be at your neighborhood supermarket.

The heart of the program is a set of four DVDs with the instructions and specialized workouts. There is also a bonus "Fitness Concert" for those of you who are more advanced. It's great to go to a live class, but in the winter that can be hard. There are also advantages to dancing around your own room. (no embarrassment when you trip over your own feet)

I love this! When New years resolutions involve fun, they're more likely to get done.
text_fidelity_b: Zumba Fitness Tone Up DVD System

text_fidelity_a:
Backyard Champs Cornhole Carry Bag If you own a cornhole set, you are well aware of the need to transport the set from your garage to your backyard, basement to car, etc. You could just carry the boards and bean bags the way they are, but a better option is to store the set in a carrying bag. And a good choice for the task is the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag.

I got hold of this bag at the same time that I obtained a cornhole set, also from Backyard Champs. The idea of a carrying bag made sense, so I added it to my order. The bag is black in color and seals shut with Velcro flaps. It measures two feet in width, four feet in length, and eight inches in thickness. Thus, it has enough space to hold the cornhole set I own, which is from the same company. However, it may not be the correct size for other sets, so make sure you measure first.

The carrying handles on this bag are a little thinner than expected. They are also looped more widely than I feel they should be. A little less width, more like a briefcase handle, would seem better. The cornhole set I have isn’t too heavy so I think the handles will hold up, but there is still a little more looseness than I prefer. I hope I am proven wrong and that the manufacturer knew what they were doing when they designed the bag, but it just seems a little too loose for me. I suppose they made the loop larger so that you can place the handle over your shoulder but I prefer to carry it more like a suitcase.

Cornhole sets are often bulky and they need to be protected when transporting from one place to another. A carrying bag makes sense and the Backyard Champs 2 x 4 Cornhole Carry Bag is a good choice for the task. A little more snug fit and a separate compartment for the bean bags would make this bag better, but it is a good enough bag for the job.
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Champs Cornhole Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer) We have three sets of kitchen knives; a low quality TV infomercial special, a medium quality Chicago Cutlery set, and what we consider high quality home knives by J.A. Henckels. Plus we have more working knives than I care to count. I have used a lot of sharpeners and edge straighteners over the decades but we only use those now for machetes that my wife won't let me use in the Chef's Choice 120. They'd fit too!

I bought the 120 for my wife two years after I bought her the J.A. Henckels knives. New, the knives were amazing; felt like they had a near surgical edge. I knew once they got dull or burred we didn't have anything that would restore them to like-new condition. Before we bought the 120 we took our dull Chicago Cutlery knives to a professional butcher for sharpening to see what we'd get back. We were not impressed with the results so I knew we needed to find a good knife sharpener.

After reading the reviews on sharpeners, I chose the Chef's Choice 120. We carefully read the directions and practiced our technique on the cheap knives. Wow, talk about impressed with the results. Then we put the dull Chicago Cutlery knives through all three stages on the 120. Several of the knives were so dull we had to three-stage them three times to recover the edge. When we were finished they sliced effortlessly through paper! They had NEVER been that sharp, even new. They are decades old knives and I will admit the 1st stage of the 120 did put some scratches on the blades about 1/4" up from the edge, but we didn't care. We just wanted a razor sharp edge on the old knives and the 120 delivered.

We tested stage two and three on some loose knives we had to see if those stages scratched the knife blade. They didn't. Most knives that are maintained properly only require stage two and three, or only stage 3. Once we were confident of no scratches we used only the Stage 3 polishing strop stage on the newer J.A. Henckels. Although the knives were two years old and still exceptionally sharp, they had not been sharpened since we bought them. Plus they had developed a few small burrs. The 120 Stage 3 strop stage removed the burrs, restored the near surgical, like-new edge, and no scratches either. My wife was thrilled with the results!

We use the Stage 3 strop stage on several serrated knives we own and they are noticeably improved and shaper. I've used the 120 on my working pocket knives too. I thought they were acceptably sharp using a diamond edge straightener but the 120 takes sharpening to a completely new level.

The 120 will get hot sharpening a bunch of knives one right after the other, but we typically limit our sharpening to ten knives or less. Stage 1 definitely does scratch the blade but that stage is only recommended for hopelessly dull knives.

Others may have issues with the 120. Not us. Once you understand the technique you need to use with the sharpener, it works great! We love it!
text_fidelity_b: Chef'sChoice Knife Sharpener (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

This is a thick plastic spork that is just somewhat stronger than a typical plastic utensil. It is BPA-free and is food and dishwasher safe. I got this because many times when I go on a staycation, I pack a cooler with yogurt and stuff for day travel. This is perfect for that. A butter knife cuts better. However, the spoon and fork are good for any "away-type" eating such as camping, backpacking, or just a staycation with a cooler in tow.

Even though the price is right, the reason I give this 3 stars is because the knife is useless and the thick plastic has a different mouth feel and pick-up ability. For instance, when I was eating yogurt with the spoon, I could not scrape the container as easily with the spoon end as I could with the [[ASIN:B07M8K5VQ8 Titanium Spork]]. Anyway, the outside of the palm side of the glove has leather patches over the base of fingers and thumb, along the edge of the hand, and at the ends of each finger. This gives a good grip and protects your hand. The glove material doesn't look particularly sweat-absorbent, yet my hand didn't get sweaty-slick while doing hard exercise with these on.

Gifts for Men Survival Kit, 15 in 1 Mens Accessories Emergency Survival Gear and Equipment Tool Set Outdoor, Cool Gadgets for Adventure Lovers Christmas Stocking Stuffers Idea 13 of the 15 items are equal to, or higher quality than expected. You get what you should and it's manufactured correctly. Going to start this with my three complaints and then work to what's good.

I do not consider the spoon-fork-knife done right, it's got a whistle built in that there's no way to whistle (I mean, the thing does include a whistle as well so this isn't a major concern.) I could get a little hiss out of it but it's not in whistle use category. Maybe it's just a whistle shaped air hole, but I doubt it.

Flashlight ships with no battery... you know you're going to give this to someone, it's going to sit in their car until they need it, and then bam... make sure you put in a battery and check it. It's a very low light unit, but you know what not a huge deal just something you need to include and remember to include or you're sans survival tool.

What I really wanted out of this was a multi-tool that could be used. This one is usable, but it's excessively thin. Most things in this kit are pretty useful level, but that multi-tool... survive I get it, not thrive.

One of the specific groups targeted in the advertising is cyclists. Interestingly this is what got me to get this due to having used keys the day I ordered it to work on a bike that was about 5 miles from anywhere when it threw a chain. Let's say this is probably not for cyclist. That multi-tool is... let's say I generally carry a good one and it's not, which is sad considering most of this stuff is really at least decent.

So - get a battery, wrap said battery in one of the plastic bags this came with so it doesn't explode in the flashlight, replace the multi tool or pack a screwdriver if you're going to need to work on a bike, it's a fine addition to your camping trip or something to keep with you in the car in the event of an emergency. Case is pretty cheap feeling but you know what, survival...

Oh yeah, the knife is better than expected... it's ridiculously light however so be aware it doesn't feel right, doesn't grip like ones that look like it.

Tommaso Avventura - Holiday Special Pricing - Shimano Sora Gravel Adventure Bike with Disc Brakes, Extra Wide Tires, and Carbon Fork, Road Or Dirt Trail Touring, Matte Black Usage : Everyday commute, weekend long trips.

This is my first bike after about 10 years. Overall I am pleased with the bike.

Cons:
- It runs on the heavier side and you can feel the weight, but I could not find anything much lighter in similar dollar range. Again it's not too heavy. I carried the bike after an accident for about 2 miles.
- Carrying the bike isn't the easiest. I wish the ergonomics allowed for that better.
- Seat could be a little softer but it's not the bike's fault. You can easily find a better seat. I have used the seat for longer rides and it gets painful after about 2 hours for me. So not bad at all.

Pros:
- The brakes are really good. They can bring you to a halt in a pretty high grade descent really fast if you need that to happen. Of course they need tuning and maintenance like anything else.
- The handlebars are very comfortable. I loved the overall handling of the bike.
- Riding it is fun. I went for a 5 hour ride. The bike maintained it's fun except the hard seat.
- Giantnerd's ready to ride made it possible to get this bike rolling out in 20 mins. Highly recommended.

Overall, I would highly recommend this bike to someone who is new, is on budget or needs a bike for daily commute and occasional long rides. So basically everyone except pros could use this bike.

1) beautiful packaging - attractive sturdy box, professional labeling, etc. Does not seem like a typical mass-produced "China Special."

2) good design - two hand warmer in one, with a magnetic connections that keeps them together.

3) comes with carrying pouch

4) rechargeable

5) available in different colors

6) you get TWO hand warmers in one - perfect for those of us who have two hands, two pockets to keep warm, etc.

7) they feel sturdy yet are relatively lightweight.

Now the bad news: the first set I received worked well ONCE. The second time around, one of the halves wouldn't charge.

I requested a replacement through Amazon and returned the first set.

After 3 uses, one of the "halves" in the second set stopped receiving a charge as well. Thus, this set is going back to Amazon.

The concept of rechargeable hand warmers is great. However, the technology itself seems to need refinement, especially when it comes to recharging.

I had this same issue with another brands so I'm thinking it's a "category of goods" issue.

Brazos Trekking Pole,Hiking Pole,Hiking Stick,Walking Stick That Collapses and Folds to 27 Inches and Adjusts in Height from 43-53 inches with Non Shock Technology and Interchangeable Tips,Set of 2 I've never used a walking/trekking stick before, so I can't compare these with others. However, I really wish they'd included some directions as it's an experimental, hit-and-miss method of trying to use them. Also, one of the two sticks won't lock. One stick is fine--I could unscrew the pole (twist the pole, not the black part between the segments), pull the length out, and screw until locked on both the bottom and top segments of the stick. It only took about 4-5 twists to unlock and then again to lock this pole. The second one locks on the bottom section, but that's only tall enough for a child. The top portion won't lock even after being twisted in the lock direction for several minutes. That stick decreases in height with every step and so is useless, thus the low star rating. I can unlock and collapse both poles without problem.

The tip can be used with a 1" textured, rubber tip attachment for sidewalks and such. This tip simply pulls off to expose the permanent, (3/16" across) tungsten carbide tip. A 2" wide plastic disk can be slipped over the tip and screwed into place about 2" up the pole to prevent the stick from sinking too far in sand. There is an adjustable, padded wrist strap. The sticks are a lightweight metal and seem reasonably sturdy. You have to keep track of any tip attachments when not using them as they don't come with a pouch or container.

XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination Since I turned my bike into a commuter vehicle, I've been looking to replace my existing light with a road and pedestrian friendly.

I was looking for a light that had a cutoff like a automotive headlight. I found that there was a standard called STVZO that fell onto that category. I also saw that many of these light were rather expensive. So I was surprised to find this on being that is was fairly inexpensive compare to similar lights.

Comparatively, this one is noticeably larger then my current light. Well, the first thing I tried after taking it out of the box, was to charge it. I plugged in one of my existing USB C cables and could not charge it. My plug was too big to fully seat. I was able to use the cable that was in the packaging. So be aware of that consideration. The port cover fits tightly and takes a little bit of effort to pop open.

I chose the handle bar mount. The mount doesn't rotate laterally and thus not vulnerable to snapping off at the pivot light other handle bar mounted lights.

I have a standard size extender and the mount needs to be tightened all the way to get a good cinch. Unfortunately, that means the long screw sticks up and blocks the light from sliding on. So I need to add some rubber strips to remove the slack.

The manual vs motion mode was a little confusing at first. I opted to go with manual mode to keep it on while I'm at a traffic stop.

Well, the proof us in the pudding. The beam pattern has a clear and distinct cut off. It's also bright and has a good spread. At this price point, this is a great value for a quality light.

Overall, I'm really happy with using this light while riding at night. The issue of the loose mount and small USB port could be improved upon, but it still get's the job done.
text_fidelity_b: XOSS Smart Bike Headlight, 800 Lumens Super Bright Bicycle Light, USB Rechargeable Bike Light Front with 5 Light Modes, Water Resistant, Safety for Mountain, Kids, Street, Bikes Camping Illumination

Slime 10056W Bike Tube Puncture Repair Sealant, Prevent and Repair, Suitable for All Bicycles, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly, 16oz Bottle Used it, Loved it ... on the single wheel on my electric unicycle (EUC).
Where the rubber meets the road, it seems, doesn't get enough love here. So I thought I'd start a thread to share opinions about tire pressure, maintenance, etc. (starting with some of my opinions).

I find tire pressure to be one of the most important components of handling and ride, and I'm a bit obsessive about it on my EUC's (probably carrying over from motorcycles and bikes). There are three things that make tire pressure a challenge with EUC's:

EUC's only have one tire, low pressure has a direct impact on ride, and tire failures are unforgiving
EUC's have unique bent valve stems that make it hard to find inner-tubes, and a pain to fill (you just don't want to do it)
EUC tire pressure is a bother to check compared to any other vehicle, because the valve stems are hidden in the EUC cavity, and difficult to attach to a pump
... and there are probably other things. The net result is that you want to maintain the tire, fill to pressure and forget it.

To that end, I've Slimed (https://www.amazon.com/Slime-10056-Tube-Sealant-oz/dp/B003V9XYNW/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1487706156&sr=8-2&keywords=slime+bicycle) both my V8 and Zero. I used about 1/3rd of the bottle on each one. There is no effect whatsoever on the feel of the wheel, and I think it provides a certain security. In Chicago, I can take my bike into any number of convenient shops to buy and install a new inner-tube; but the same shops would just draw a blank with an EUC, and the inner-tubes are hard to find. Best to maintain what you have.

I like to keep my tire pressure up at 3 bar (~44 psi). The sidewalls of my V8 and Zero tires both recommend 40-65psi pressure, and the V8 comes from the factory at 2.8 bar (~40psi). So for me 3 bar seems the right pressure, and both wheels feel good at that pressure. It's a real bother to fit a pressure gauge on the valve stem because they are bent against the wheel. I almost never get a seal on my gauge without several tries.

So instead, I pumped the wheels up with my Lezyne pump (https://www.amazon.com/Lezyne-Steel-Floor-Drive-Black/dp/B005UND3CY/ref=sr_1_3?ie=UTF8&qid=1487706504&sr=8-3&keywords=lezyne+pump) -- I recommend Lesyzne as the absolute best bike pump on the market -- and then put a Gozens 44psi cap (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01HRIKIY0/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) on the wheel. That way, I can easily check the pressure at the start of each ride. You do need to buy the Gozens at a particular pressure (BTW, they have bluetooth systems, which I think are a bit of overkill) but you get 4 of the basic caps for $9, so NBD.
text_fidelity_b: Slime 10056W Bike Tube Puncture Repair Sealant, Prevent and Repair, Suitable for All Bicycles, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly, 16oz Bottle

Franklin Sports Pickleball Paddle - X-1000 Polypropylene Core Pickleball Racket - Official USA Pickleball (USAPA) Approved Pickleball Paddle - Lightweight Pro Racket - 8mm Thick Core Ok, if your unfamiliar with the game of Pickleball, some people take it very seriously despite the name. It's a combination of tennis, badminton and table tennis that can be played as singles or doubles on a 20' by 44' Court.
The paddle is the most important part of the game and ranges in size and weight. The weight starts at 6oz and goes up to 14oz. The handles vary in size and you can measure starting at the tip of your middle finger to your palm to see the appropriate size you need.
The lighter the paddle the more control you have over the ball but it offers less drive (power) on the ball. On the positive side the lighter weight also offers less wear and tear on your elbow/wrist/arm and is best if you are a beginner.
It's a fun game and even if you don't start out playing on a court or even with a net its good exercise, practice for hand eye coordination and mental flexibility.
This Franklin paddle is more than sufficient and at only 7.7 oz. offers a lighter weight combined with the polypropylene core which offers extra power and stability.
The handle on this X1000 is 4" and runs on the smaller side of the spectrum.

text_fidelity_a:
Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update) Picked up this tent after LOTS of searching and watching reviews. This tent is heavier than what I wanted for backpacking, however, I think the trade offs will be positive.
First off, the construction is very good out of the bag. All seams and tie out points are sealed with seam tape. No loose threads. The fly and tub are manufactured with a nice weight nylon, not too thin, and not too thick.
The newly designed corner sleeves for the poles are nice, this helps to pull the tent body nice and taut. Great design.
I like the color scheme as well, not too bright, but not drab either.
The aluminum pole segments seem to be shorter than most other tents, this should make it easy to pack in my back pack. I still have not decided if I will roll everything up in the storage bag and pack it vertically. Or use a stuff sack and shove the tent in the bottom of my pack and store the poles on the outside of the pack.
The vestibule is nice. It is not huge, but, it has plenty of room for shoes and some other items that you do not want to store in the tent. The ONE thing that sold me on this tent, is the way the vestibule zips open and closed. The last dome style I had with a vestibule, it zipped right down the middle. This made it hard to get to, as you had to basically crawl most of the way out of the tent to unzip it. This vestibule unzips right at the side of the entrance, which makes it super easy to open and close! AWESOME design!! More tent manufacturers need to use this design.
The only two cons I have right out of the packaging, is:
1. The tent IS on the heavy side, at almost 5 pounds. But, if you were backpacking with a friend or spouse, you could split up the pieces and make it lighter. But for a solo hiker, it is heavy. However, with the room you get, it is a good trade off.
2. The fly tie downs were just short loops of cordage that did not even reach the ground, and you cannot use the stakes to stake them out. Both sides and the rear are like this. I fixed this issue by just adding a length of cordage to all 3 spots.
I removed the supplied plastic line adjusters and just tied a taut line hitch on all pieces of cordage.
I will update after a few uses if need be.
text_fidelity_b: Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update)

text_fidelity_a:
Timex Personal Trainer Heart Rate Monitor Watch - Gray I had purchased this as a Christmas gift, but my wife thought she might be allergic to the chest strap. So I am using it. The watch and chest strap are well made. Here are some things you should know:

1. you must use the chest strap. You get no heart/pulse rate readings on the watch without it. The chest strap is easy on, easy off.
2. once you affix the chest strap, you will forget you have it on.
3. you need to wet a portion of the chest strap before applying it for the day. I simply put a swipe of water on each part of the strap on either side of the Timex logo. You only need do this once per day, or so I have found.
4. while you can change the battery in the chest strap yourself, the manual recommends a professional change the watch battery.
5. the manual itself requires some close attention if you are to get the full benefit of the monitor. I am still figuring out all of the bells and whistles.
6. the recorded HR on this watch matches the treadmill HR monitor at the gym as well as our BP machine.

When I read that other reviewers bought this item based on their heart doctor's suggestion, I thought that was good enough for me. My wife's loss is my gain (smile)!

UPDATE, March 14,2013
I continue to enjoy the use of this product immensely. Note that when you are not using the HR monitor feature, it serves as a timepiece. And finally, a note to those who, like me, are hearing impaired. On the first day I used this monitor, I went to see my hearing aid dispenser for a check-up. He immediately said, "What's beeping?" I said, is it my phone? He said no, it seems to be coming from . . . there. He meant the monitor on my wrist! I myself could not hear it a lick! So: if you see a tiny chime icon on the watch face in monitor mode, then anyone close to you can hear what I surmise are rhythmic beeps. The chime feature can be turned off, as I discovered after I spent a half-day announcing my presence to the world!
text_fidelity_b: Timex Personal Trainer Heart Rate Monitor Watch - Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Lezyne Road Drive HP High Pressure Road Bike Hand Pump, 160psi, Presta Valve Only, Gravel, Track Bicycle Over the decades of commuting, racing and just fun riding I've owned too many frame/mini pumps. Frame fit Silca Impero was still the standard against a handful of Zefals, Crank Brothers used. New top pump is the Lezyne Road Drive large size.

Strokes to reach and level of effort at 100psi:
Road Drive= 150 strokes at an easy-moderate effort
Pressure Drive (med) = 140 strokes at a moderate-hard effort
Silca Impero 520mm size = 120 strokes (90psi) at hard effort

The Road Drive is ~3mm narrower than the Pressure Drive. Maybe why it takes less effort at any psi above 70. Longer stroke more or less made up for the difference in air volume delivered.

The Lezyne pumps required a threaded valve stem. The pump is connected to the valve stem by a flexible length of hose that screws onto the pump when in use. Stored within the pump. Reduces the chance of snapping off a valve stem.

text_fidelity_a:
BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids. I purchased this to use on my bicycle that I use for commuting. I leave early in the morning while it is still dark. The route I take is pretty well lit with street lights so I use the lights mostly for visibility and not to light the road in front of me.

The mounts are pretty simple to use. I attached the front to the handlebar and the back to the basket I have on the rear rack. The front light has 3 steady settings at 3 levels of brightness and one flashing mode. I am not sure how useful the level of brightness would be in absolute darkness as far as seeing the path in front of you because I have not used it in that scenario, but it seems pretty bright to me. I keep it on flashing mode for visibility. It is conveniently re-chargeable via USB cord and it seems to last adequately between charges.

I gave this product a 3 star rating because the back light does not work the way I need it to. The first time I used it, I thought I turned it on but when I got to my destination it was off so I figured I forgot to turn it on. The second time I used it on the return trip, I made absolutely sure it was on when I started and when I got to the destination it was off again. I took the light off my bike and turned it on and dropped it onto a hard surface from a distance of less than 3 inches and it shut off. Since this is battery operated and not rechargeable, I'm guessing the batteries get jolted from going over a bump on the road and shuts off on its own. It lights up again without any issues if you press the on button again, but that is not feasible or safe to reach behind you and fix it if you are riding on a road with vehicular traffic all around you. It is also very inconvenient to pull over to the side every time it shuts off to turn it back on again. Since the light set was fairly inexpensive, I just purchased a different separate backlight from the local box store to replace it.

I will not go through the time and inconvenience of returning the item or exchanging it because it simply is not worth it. I hope the seller doesn't try to contact me to "fix" the problem because they will be wasting their time.
text_fidelity_b: BLITZU 2023 Bike Lights Set with Bell USB-C Rechargeable. Bicycle Accessories for Night Riding, Cycling. Powerful Front Headlight, Back Rear LED Taillight. Road Safety for Men, Women, Kids.

text_fidelity_a:
Texan Classics Utility Hybrid Iron-Wood #2 Golf Club OK - my own fault as by now, I know you get what you pay for. On this basis, buying a $20 hybrid is more experiment than sensible purchase. But based on prior reviews, I thought, why not?

Here's why not: I received the club on Wednesday, put it in my bag and went to the course on Thursday. Looks like a Taylormade Rescue, but with really poor detail. Well, looks don't get the ball down the course, and it was $20, so who cares, right?

First shot, nicely impressed...second shot, the same. Third shot, I feel something...odd. Ball pops straight up in the air at almost a 90 degree angle to my lie. Look at the club, and there's the answer. Clubhead is an inch down the shaft from the ferrule, and with the slightest tug, it pops right off. So much for the experiment.

Maybe I'm crazy, but there's just no excuse for a clubhead falling off within three shots; six swings total with practice. None. Zero. I'm surprised it actually made it through shipping without coming off. Maybe they used cornstarch to glue this on instead of epoxy? Who knows. The only saving grace is that I hadn't yet thrown away the box, so it was easy to return this dismal thing.
text_fidelity_b: Texan Classics Utility Hybrid Iron-Wood #2 Golf Club

Etekcity Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Accessories Gear Tent Lights, Lanterns Battery Powered LED for Power Outages, Survival Kits, Operated Lamp, 4 Pack This small lantern is a little less than 5 1/2" tall and about 3 1/2" in diameter. If you need smaller, then you need a flashlight! As for light, it has plenty! I have 2 LED lanterns 10" tall by 5" dia. and they put out half as much light as these smaller ones. My bigger ones are not efficient enough to read by, these are. I need these strictly for outages, which we seem to have a lot of, and I appreciate the area coverage of these. No, it will not make it easy to read a few feet away from them, no lantern does that, but it will make it easy to see and navigate in a 15' x 15' room.
They are adjustable in only one way, and that is how much you open them. (At just high enough to turn them on, they make great guiding lights for a footpath or a cluttered area.) All the bulbs are on no matter how close to closed it is, so there is no power saving advantage to having it lowered. 12 Hours of emergency or evening lighting outside, is a lot of hours! It will more than stand up to all emergency needs except getting lost in a cave! LOL If it only had 3-4 hours of good light, I would not be happy with this, my first thought is always 'how to extend the emergency light time' and 'is it adjustable'. Well, you can't, and its not....Because of that this would not be an economic idea for an extended camping trip. But this is not being touted as a night after night lighting fix, as an emergency light, I don't need to worry about that.
I joined Etekcity's review program, because I have purchased several of their products and haven't found one I didn't appreciate a lot! As such I don't feel bad about getting one of their products at a reduced price or free for reviewing them. I take my time, and look at all the negative reviews and see if any apply to the product i received. So far.... yes it is pretty light, but no it would not blow away in less that 50mph winds. And i don't think you would be outside enjoying an evening in that kind of wind anyway. It has the hard anodized look and feeling of a well coated flashlight. The handles are wide enough to be easy to carry and a bungee cord or rope will attach them to the side of any tree or post, or you can hang them from a limb or tent pole. Heavy enough not to tip over, and good quality plastic instead of glass or cheep plastic that cracks. I don't see anything cheap or flimsy feeling about them at all!
Don't know what else to say about these, except my other two larger ones are going out into storage and I will be getting 2 more of these to store inside for emergencies. I highly recommend them!
PS: If you DO get a lemon, for Pete's sake tell them! They are very quick and easy to talk to. There is a card in the box with a toll free number, their e-mail address and their website on it (etekcity.com).... all for customer support.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Accessories Gear Tent Lights, Lanterns Battery Powered LED for Power Outages, Survival Kits, Operated Lamp, 4 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Smarthealth Walking Fit Activity Tracker - Black - Large I was really looking for a way to kick start some healthier habits and this watch and the 10,000 steps program seemed to be a perfect match. I'm a couple months in and I can say without a doubt that I am noticeably more in shape than I was when this watch came in the mail.

As for the 10,000 steps program, you could not get easier. If you haven't gotten your steps in, walk until you do. It is low impact but the results are tangiable for those of us who have spent too much time in our cubicles.

The watch itself is pretty easy to use. I had no problems setting the watch and the function buttons are pretty straightforward. The few problems I do have with it are that the strap is tight and tends to pinch and pull arm hairs. Also on occasion it seems to miss steps unless you are actively swinging your arm. It seemed like I was swinging my arms in a little exaggerated motion for a while, but now it feels like I'm engaging my upper body while walking.

Pros
+ Absolutely simple entry to healthier activity
+ Encoraging to keep going to meet your goal
+ It tells time, right there on your arm, no need to pull your phone out.

Cons
- Band is a little tight, or at the next step, a little loose.
- Not a Con, but I find I don't use the heart rate monitor
- Auto resets at midnight - I work second shift so that is not ideal so I set it to shift at noon. Perhaps that can be changed.
- I misplaced it for a couple days and missed it.

Summary
I'll be modest about what this watch has done for me. I'm not going to South Beach based on the 10,000 steps. But when I walk out my front door to go to work, I feel stronger legs. I see definition as fat has been going down and muscles are firming up. It's not an instant cure, but I see it as, in six weeks I can look and feel better, the same or worse. In the first six weeks I can say that this has definitely made me feel and look better. Bring on the next six weeks.
text_fidelity_b: Smarthealth Walking Fit Activity Tracker - Black - Large

Biscuits & Gravy | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings I was really surprised at how well they hit the exact flavor and consistency that I love from biscuits and gravy with this meal! This was my first mountain house dehydrated meal that I have ever eaten, and I learned a lot from testing it out. I actually picked up a few flavors in the last couple weeks just to taste them and know which ones I would actually like to bring backpacking or keep in my emergency supply kit.

What I learned from this is that I need to make sure that my water is seriously boiling hot and not just boiled five minutes ago. I also need to measure extremely carefully and definitely not short it on water. And also I need to not worry about the meal getting soggy, and instead taste a bite, and close the packet again and let it soak in some more if that is not fully rehydrated.

Overall, this was a perfect introduction to how fresh and delicious food like this can taste. We actually had some garden zucchini to eat on the side, and so having the biscuits and gravy, a fried egg, and some garden zucchini, all able to be cooked up on the camping stove, was amazing! It felt like a full, amazing meal, and even if I didn't have the egg or zucchini available, I would've been very happy to eat this.

In addition, there are some types of wheat that really bother me, and I wanted to find out if the wheat used in this product gave me that specific allergic reaction that I get to so many, even high quality, foods. I was absolutely delighted to find out that I did not experience any of the itching, swollen eyes, or other sensations that I occasionally get from eating wheat from certain brands. I am now feeling more confident to test out different flavors from this brand and definitely will include this specific flavor in my camping and emergency supply box. The portion size was enough to feed both myself, and my four and six-year-old kids, with accessory foods on the side to fill out the meal.
text_fidelity_b: Biscuits & Gravy | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings

Sleeping Bag, Ohuhu Lightweight Sleeping Bag 3 Season Warm Weather Portable Compact Sleeping Bags for Adult Kids with Carry Bag for Camping Hiking Backpacking and Outdoors 59℉-77℉ For the price, this is a pretty well-made sleeping bag. It's very lightweight, so it's not something you'd want to use in the winter (or even fall) but for more temperate times of the year, it performs well. It's also great for "indoor camping" or sleepovers since it's so lightweight and easy to tote.

The zipper is a critical point and, while this is not a real heavy-duty zipper, it's better than the ones I've seen on other similar sleeping bags. You do need to work the zipper slowly to ensure you don't get the fabric caught in the teeth, but the overall zipper build quality and action is better than I expected. It's a two-way zipper, so you can unzip the base, but keep the side zipped up.

The fabric is poly and is very smooth to the touch. I didn't find any loose threads or puckered seams. The fill is also 100% poly, and is nicely distributed without any lumps or bunches. While the fill is thin, I found it pretty comfortable to sleep in provided that you use a ground pad.

The only negative, and the reason for the loss of one star, is the carry pouch. It's very small. That's good since when you get the sleeping bag into the carry pouch, it takes up surprisingly little room. However, getting the sleeping bag back into the pouch is a real chore. You have to fold the bag up, then roll it very, very tightly to stand even a small chance of getting it to fit into the pouch. The straps on the carry pouch are also rather finicky to adjust. A slightly larger pouch, with better straps, would be a big improvement.

The pouch aside, this is a good lightweight bag that is priced well, but still has decent build quality. Well worth considering.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sleeping Bag, Ohuhu Lightweight Sleeping Bag 3 Season Warm Weather Portable Compact Sleeping Bags for Adult Kids with Carry Bag for Camping Hiking Backpacking and Outdoors 59℉-77℉
